senses.gloss: To knock a person or animal unconscious with a blow or an electric shock.
examples: The blow to the head *stunned* him for several seconds.
Officers carry devices that *stun* rather than kill.
The bird was *stunned* by the window and lay still on the grass.

senses.gloss: To make a feeling, a sound, or a color less strong.
examples: She *subdued* her anger and answered politely.
Soft lighting can *subdue* the mood of a whole room.
The music was *subdued* so that guests could hear each other.

senses.gloss: To stop resisting and accept someone else's power or authority.
examples: He refused to *submit* to the guards.
The city finally *submitted* after a long siege.
Having *submitted* to a search, she was waved through.

senses.gloss: To take over a position or a title from the person who held it before.
senses.ru: сменять на посту, стать преемником; наследовать (престол)
examples: She *succeeded* him as head of the department.
Nobody knows who will *succeed* the current governor.
He has *succeeded* his father as owner of the farm.

senses.gloss: To be very bad or very unpleasant, in informal speech.
examples: This weather *sucks*.
The movie *sucked*, but the popcorn was good.
Losing your wallet on the first day of vacation really *sucks*.

senses.gloss: To be a sign that something is probably true.
senses.ru: указывать на, свидетельствовать о; наводить на мысль
examples: The numbers *suggest* that prices will fall again.
Her tone *suggested* she was not convinced.
Early tests have *suggested* a link between the two drugs.

senses.gloss: To gather your strength, courage, or energy for something difficult.
examples: It takes time to *summon* that kind of courage.
She *summoned* her last bit of strength and pushed the door open.
*Summoning* what patience he had left, he asked again.

senses.gloss: To hold the weight of something and keep it from falling.
examples: Four stone columns *support* the roof.
The old shelf *supported* far more weight than it should have.
The walkway is *supported* by steel cables.

senses.gloss: To provide someone with the money they need to live.
examples: He *supports* a family of five on one salary.
She *supported* herself through college by waiting tables.
Their parents have *supported* them for years.

senses.gloss: For a device or a program to be able to work with something.
examples: My phone doesn't *support* that app anymore.
The older model never *supported* wireless charging.
That file type is no longer *supported*.

senses.gloss: To ride ocean waves standing on a board.
senses.ru: заниматься сёрфингом, кататься на доске по волнам
examples: They *surf* every morning before work.
He *surfed* the North Shore all summer.
She has been *surfing* since she was six years old.

senses.gloss: To move forward suddenly as one large mass, like a crowd or a wave.
senses.ru: хлынуть, устремляться вперёд; накатывать (о волне, толпе)
examples: The crowd *surged* toward the stage.
Water *surges* through the gate the moment it opens.
Fans were *surging* onto the field before the whistle blew.

senses.gloss: To come upon someone suddenly when they do not expect it.
examples: The homeowner *surprised* a burglar in the kitchen.
They planned to *surprise* the camp at dawn.
The guards were *surprised* in their sleep.

senses.gloss: To ask a group of people a set of questions in order to collect their opinions.
examples: The company *surveyed* two thousand shoppers.
Researchers plan to *survey* teachers in every state.
Of those *surveyed*, half said they would move.

senses.gloss: To measure and record the exact shape and boundaries of a piece of land.
examples: A crew came out to *survey* the property line.
They *surveyed* the valley before the road was built.
The lot has never been properly *surveyed*.

senses.gloss: To remain alive after another person has died.
senses.ru: пережить (кого-либо), остаться в живых после чьей-то смерти
examples: She is *survived* by two sons and a sister.
He *survived* his wife by ten years.
Nobody expected the youngest brother to *survive* them all.

senses.gloss: To hang something so that it is held up from above.
examples: The crew *suspended* the camera above the stage.
They will *suspend* the platform from four cables.
Tiny particles stay *suspended* in the liquid for hours.

senses.gloss: To suffer an injury, a loss, or damage.
examples: Two passengers *sustained* minor injuries in the crash.
A helmet keeps riders from *sustaining* head injuries.
The company has *sustained* heavy losses this year.

senses.gloss: For a judge to accept an objection or a claim as valid.
examples: The judge *sustained* the defense's objection.
If the court *sustains* the claim, the city will owe damages.
Her objection was *sustained* and the question was withdrawn.

senses.gloss: To believe something that is not true.
examples: I'm not going to *swallow* that excuse.
They *swallowed* the whole story without asking a single question.
He had *swallowed* every word of it.

senses.gloss: To hold back a feeling instead of showing it.
examples: She *swallowed* her pride and asked for help.
You learn to *swallow* your anger in this job.
He has *swallowed* a lot of insults from that man.

senses.gloss: To give someone far more work, calls, or requests than they can handle.
examples: Complaints *swamped* the customer service line.
I'm *swamped* until Friday.
One bad review can *swamp* a small shop with questions.

senses.gloss: To influence someone's opinion or decision.
senses.ru: склонять, склонить (к мнению); влиять на, переубеждать
examples: Nothing I said could *sway* her.
His speech *swayed* a few undecided voters.
The jury was *swayed* by the photographs.

senses.gloss: To make an offer or a deal more attractive.
examples: They *sweetened* the offer with two extra vacation days.
The city may *sweeten* the deal to keep the factory.
The contract was *sweetened* at the last minute.

senses.gloss: To slide a finger across a touchscreen.
senses.ru: проводить пальцем по экрану, смахивать, листать
examples: *Swipe* left to delete the message.
She *swiped* through her photos the whole train ride.
He kept *swiping* at the screen with wet hands.

senses.gloss: To steal something small, in informal speech.
examples: Someone *swiped* my umbrella from the hallway.
Don't leave your phone where a kid can *swipe* it.
Half the candy had been *swiped* before the party started.

senses.gloss: To hit out at something with a quick sweeping movement.
examples: The cat *swiped* at my hand.
A bear can *swipe* hard enough to break bone.
He was *swiping* at flies with a dish towel.

senses.gloss: To copy data between two devices so that both hold the same information.
examples: My phone *syncs* with my laptop automatically.
I *synced* the calendar before the flight.
The files have not *synced* since Tuesday.

senses.gloss: To make a substance artificially by combining chemicals.
examples: The lab can *synthesize* the drug in three steps.
Chemists first *synthesized* the compound in 1952.
Vitamin D is *synthesized* in the skin.

senses.gloss: To knock or pull someone to the ground, especially in football.
senses.ru: сбивать с ног, повалить; блокировать (в футболе)
examples: He was *tackled* a yard short of the goal line.
Two officers *tackled* the man in the parking lot.
She learned to *tackle* without leading with her helmet.

senses.gloss: To touch another player in a chasing game, or to touch a runner with the ball in baseball.
senses.ru: осалить, запятнать (в игре); коснуться мячом (в бейсболе)
examples: *Tag* someone and then they're it.
He *tagged* her and ran off laughing.
The runner was *tagged* a step before he reached third.

senses.gloss: To eat and drink in a stadium parking lot before a game.
senses.ru: устраивать пикник на парковке перед матчем
examples: We always *tailgate* before home games.
They *tailgated* in the north lot for three hours.
Half the crowd was still *tailgating* at kickoff.

senses.gloss: To give information to the police or an enemy, especially under pressure.
examples: The suspect finally *talked*.
They were afraid he would *talk*.
Nobody in the crew has *talked* yet.

senses.gloss: To listen secretly to someone's phone calls through a hidden connection.
examples: Agents *tapped* his home phone for a year.
It is illegal to *tap* a line without a warrant.
Their calls were being *tapped* the whole time.

senses.gloss: To choose someone for a job or an honor.
examples: She was *tapped* to lead the new division.
The party *tapped* a young governor as its candidate.
They may *tap* him for the open seat.

senses.gloss: To draw liquid out of a tree, a barrel, or a container.
examples: They *tap* the maples every March.
Somebody *tapped* the keg an hour early.
These trees have been *tapped* for forty years.

senses.gloss: To record sound or video.
examples: The show is *taped* in front of a live audience.
He *taped* the whole interview on his phone.
They are *taping* two episodes today.

senses.gloss: To damage someone's good name or reputation.
examples: The scandal *tarnished* his reputation for good.
One bad review can *tarnish* a small restaurant's name.
Her record has been *tarnished* by the investigation.

senses.gloss: To make heavy demands on someone's strength, time, or patience.
examples: These meetings *tax* my patience.
The long climb *taxed* her strength.
Caring for a newborn alone is *taxing*.

senses.gloss: To give a small hint of something new in order to build interest in it.
examples: The band *teased* a new album on social media.
Studios often *tease* a sequel at the end of a film.
They have been *teasing* the announcement for weeks.

senses.gloss: To be likely to do something, or to do it regularly.
senses.ru: иметь склонность, обычно делать; быть склонным к
examples: Prices *tend* to rise in the summer.
He *tended* to arrive late, so we stopped waiting for him.
She has always *tended* toward caution.

senses.gloss: To use something in order to find out whether it works properly.
examples: Engineers *test* every battery before it ships.
They *tested* the brakes on a closed track.
The software is still being *tested*.

senses.gloss: To put a strain on someone's patience or on the limits of something.
examples: Those two *test* my patience every single day.
The delay *tested* everyone's good humor.
He has been *testing* the limits of what we will allow.

senses.gloss: To tie an animal or an object to a fixed point with a rope or a chain.
examples: The goat was *tethered* to a post behind the barn.
They *tether* the boats to iron rings on the dock.
He *tethered* the horse and went inside.

senses.gloss: To become fewer or less thick.
examples: His hair started *thinning* in his thirties.
The crowd *thinned* after the fireworks.
Traffic *thins* once you pass the second exit.

senses.gloss: To make a liquid less thick by adding water or another liquid.
examples: *Thin* the paint with a little water.
She *thinned* the sauce with a cup of stock.
The glue can be *thinned* if it gets too sticky.

senses.gloss: To be likely to harm or destroy something.
examples: The fire *threatens* two hundred homes.
Rising water *threatened* the whole village.
The species is *threatened* by the loss of its habitat.

senses.gloss: To say something in a loud, angry voice.
examples: The coach *thundered* at the referee from the sideline.
He would *thunder* at us whenever the shop was messy.
Her father was still *thundering* about the phone bill.

senses.gloss: To finish a game or a contest with the same score as the other side.
examples: If we *tie*, the match goes to penalties.
The teams *tied* 2-2 last night.
She has *tied* the world record twice.

senses.gloss: To connect a person or a thing to something else as being involved in it.
examples: DNA evidence *tied* him to the scene.
Nothing *ties* the suspect to that building.
Bonuses are *tied* to company profits.
